extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers, journal editors, authors, and readers of bibliometric/science-mapping studies
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and checklist-style guidance for evaluating bibliometric reviews and science-mapping papers, aimed at reviewers and critical readers assessing objectives, data, methods, analyses, visualizations, and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, specific, measurable objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A bibliometric analysis should not have vague or overly broad goals; objectives must focus on quantifiable data interpretation. Qualitative reasoning can be part of findings but should not be the major focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers/readers should confirm specificity and robustness of research questions (e.g., identifying influential authors, trends, collaboration networks). Check consistency between stated objectives and the analyses performed (e.g., whether conceptual/intellectual/social structure analyses align with objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification of data source selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must justify their choice of database(s) (Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, etc.) in relation to the research objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because databases have differing coverage, reviewers should evaluate whether the chosen source(s) provide appropriate coverage and whether authors acknowledge limitations and potential selection biases arising from the database choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time frame selection and cut-off date rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of time frames and cut-off dates significantly influences bibliometric trends; authors should justify the chosen period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should pay particular attention when timeframes are short (5–10 years). Authors may need to explain use of specific cut-off dates (e.g., 31 Dec vs search date) and discuss effects of early access vs indexed dates on analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and originality of contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must demonstrate how the study is relevant to the current state of the field and offer a clear rationale explaining differences from existing bibliometric reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a study merely extends a prior review by a small time span without substantive methodological or interpretive novelty, reviewers should question its contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-style transparent reporting of data cleaning (Identification stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report keywords/Boolean strings and provide reasoning for their choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check whether wildcard/hash were used to capture British/American variants and whether the search strings are documented sufficiently for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-style transparent reporting of data cleaning (Screening stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Document filters/mechanisms used to remove titles and the rationale for language or document-type inclusion/exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors limit languages or document types, they should justify these choices relative to objectives; reviewers should evaluate potential biases introduced by such filters.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA-style transparent reporting of data cleaning (Eligibility stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report how many articles were excluded and why, and discuss dataset scope/breadth limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check exclusion reasons and consider whether exclusions could bias results or interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword-level data cleaning and thesaurus use
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should standardize keywords (use of a thesaurus) to reduce ambiguous and similar terms and choose British or American English consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors fail to report keyword cleaning, co-occurrence and thematic analyses may contain redundancies; reviewers should request clarifications or thesauri used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide access to data repository
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should provide access to datasets/repositories to allow readers and reviewers to examine findings and explore further insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should request data access when absent to enable validation and reproducibility checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify multi-database use and describe integration strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: When studies use multiple bibliographic databases, authors should justify the choice and explain how data from different sources were integrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether differences in coverage, indexing policies, and metadata formats were considered and mitigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of data consistency across sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify metadata formats, perform author name disambiguation, standardize institutional affiliations, and reconcile citation counts across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes both basic metadata format checks and complex disambiguation procedures; reviewers should look for documented methods and checks used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of publication time periods across databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Align publication periods, explicitly handle early access articles, and document database update frequencies and search date stamps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time synchronization affects counts and trend detection; reviewers should ensure authors document cut-off/search dates and how early access/indexing discrepancies were handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logging/documentation of search and processing steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Log database-specific search strategies, data cleaning protocols for each source, tool-specific parameter settings, and data integration procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough logs allow reproducibility and auditing; reviewers should expect stepwise documentation of searches and transformations (parameters, thresholds, scripts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overview/result validation across platforms and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-reference key metrics across platforms, explain metric variations, validate network analyses across tools, and perform consistency checks for keyword analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discrepancies arise between tools or databases, authors should explain causes; reviewers should check cross-validation efforts rather than accepting single-tool outputs blindly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: provide raw data, step-by-step workflows, and version info
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide raw datasets where possible, detailed methodology for each tool used, a step-by-step data processing workflow, and version information for all tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproducibility requirements include code/scripts, parameter settings, and software versions; reviewers should request these if absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify and interpret time-related indexing complexities (early access vs indexed date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should consider differences between first online/accepted dates and official indexed dates and report how these affect inclusion in time-limited analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure authors discuss cases where early-access papers may be indexed in a different year and how that was managed in short time-window studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not interpret descriptive metrics in isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics like publication counts, citation counts, and h-index should not be evaluated alone; their relevance, accuracy, and interpretative depth must be critically assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should look for deeper analysis (e.g., breakdowns, normalization, complementary metrics) and contextual interpretation rather than raw counts alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate global versus local citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between total/global citations and local citations within the study dataset; recognize a paper's high global citations may not imply high influence in the niche analyzed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should provide breakdowns and reviewers should check whether analyses consider local vs global influence and discuss implications for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and justification of field/time normalization methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should justify normalization methods (e.g., MNCS, percentile-based normalization, SNIP, time-window normalization) and demonstrate appropriateness for the study context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the chosen normalization fits cross-field comparisons or longitudinal analysis and whether alternative approaches were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for h-index limitations and use complementary metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge h-index bias toward senior researchers and supplement with measures like fractionalized authorship, m-index, g-index, or first-publication year to better interpret contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ensure studies account for career-stage biases when comparing authors and consider fractional crediting or other corrective metrics where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold selection for top-N rankings and tie-breaking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of thresholds for top authors/journals/countries (e.g., top-10) can introduce bias; thresholds should be justified and tie-breaking should use secondary metrics (not alphabetical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors often present top-10 lists; reviewers should encourage consideration of appropriate thresholds (suggested top-12) and use of additional metrics (h-index, citations) to break ties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare production and citation ranks to explain discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare rank differences between production (publication counts) and citation ranking to uncover patterns or anomalies requiring explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should ask authors to interpret cases where an entity ranks highly in production but low in citations (or vice versa) to reveal insights about influence vs productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider single-country production (SCP) vs multiple-country production (MCP)
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating country-level output, differentiate SCP and MCP to understand domestic vs international collaboration contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect explicit reporting and interpretation of SCP/MCP metrics when country-level analysis is presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of particular tools and show complementarity across tools
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple analysis/visualization tools are used (VOSviewer, Bibliometrix, CiteSpace, etc.), authors should explain why each tool was chosen and how results complement one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate whether different tools add meaningful value and whether discrepancies are explained; for example, VOSviewer for visualization, Bibliometrix for statistics, CiteSpace for temporal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess conceptual structure analyses (keyword co-occurrence and thematic mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate keyword selection, standardization/elimination of redundancies, criteria for keyword types (author keyword vs keyword plus), thresholds for inclusion, and interpretability of clusters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check how authors set thresholds, labeled clusters, interpreted central vs peripheral concepts, and whether co-occurrence overemphasizes popular terms at the expense of niche topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate network visualization quality and interpretive labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Visualizations should represent distinct clusters effectively and cluster labels/interpretations must be justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should examine methods used to label clusters, whether visual density/centrality are meaningfully interpreted, and whether visuals match the narrative conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network density and centrality interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish central and peripheral concepts/actors and analyze their relationships; explain what centrality and density imply for the field's structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect authors to explain how they differentiate central/peripheral nodes and the implications for field maturity, topical prominence, or knowledge gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-maturity guidance for structural analyses (conceptual vs intellectual vs social)
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide inclusion of conceptual, intellectual, and social structure analyses based on field maturity and research objectives; conceptual structure is usually a must-have, others may be optional for emerging topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For emerging or niche topics (short time spans), social structure may not be mature enough to analyze; reviewers should judge whether the selected structural analyses match objectives and data maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate intellectual-structure analyses (co-citation, historiography)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess methods used to map intellectual structure (co-citation, historiograph) and whether they appropriately reveal knowledge flows, major trends, and foundational works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should examine node/edge thresholds, temporal slicing, and whether historiographic or co-citation results are corroborated by citation/contextual evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate social-structure analyses (collaboration networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess analyses of collaborations among authors/institutions/countries to determine patterns of influence and knowledge flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider whether collaboration networks are interpretable given dataset size and field maturity, and whether author affiliation disambiguation was properly performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and mitigate selection and algorithmic biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge selection biases at source selection, Boolean search construction, document-type choices, and software/algorithm preferences that may shape findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should expect explicit discussion of possible selection/algorithmic biases and steps taken to minimize or acknowledge their effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of performance analysis with science mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: When synthesizing performance metrics with science-mapping results, authors should provide guidance on how these complementary approaches inform one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess the logic and methods used to integrate rank/impact metrics with conceptual/intellectual maps and whether combined interpretations are coherent and justified.
